st-boar-firstaid-en-001.text:
The offline source doesn't give first-aid steps for this. In an emergency, call your local emergency number. What the source says:
Open Chest Wounds > Treatment > Making a flutter valve: Get some sort of plastic that is bigger than the wound. Ideas: credit card or similar, Ziploc bag, some first aid kits will have a ready-to-use valve. Tape the plastic patch over the wound on only 3 sides. The 4th side is left open, allowing blood to drain and air to escape. This opening should be at the bottom (as determined by the victim’s position). When the casualty inhales, the bag will be sucked in, but when the casualty exhales, the air will exit through the untaped side. [1]

st-boar-firstaid-en-002.text:
From the offline source:
External Chest Compressions: - · Compression Depth: Press down firmly and smoothly. For adults, compress the chest at least two inches (five centimeters) deep. For infants or children, compress the chest about one-third to one- half of its depth. - · Compression Rate: Perform compressions at a rate of 100 to 120 compressions per minute. This equates to about two compressions per second. - · Complete Chest Recoil: Allow the chest to fully recoil between each compression, without lifting your hands off the chest. This allows the heart to refill with blood. [1]

In an emergency, call your local emergency number (911 in the US, 112 in Europe).

Management > Rewarming: Rewarming shock (or rewarming collapse) is a sudden drop in blood pressure in combination with a low cardiac output which may occur during active treatment of a severely hypothermic person. There was a theoretical concern that external rewarming rather than internal rewarming may increase the risk. These concerns were partly believed to be due to afterdrop, a situation detected during laboratory experiments where there is a continued decrease in core temperature after rewarming has been started. Recent studies have not supported these concerns, and problems are not found with active external rewarming. [1]

st-boar-medlineplus-en-015.text:
Head injury: if they might have hurt their neck (a fall from height, a high-speed hit) or aren't responding, don't move them unless they're in danger; support the head so the head, neck and spine stay in a straight line. If they're not responding and not breathing normally, call emergency services and start CPR. If they're not responding but breathing normally, and they're vomiting or their breathing sounds blocked or gurgling, turn them on their side, keeping the head and spine in line. For a bump, hold an ice pack or frozen peas wrapped in a tea towel on it for short periods; never put ice directly on the skin. An adult should stay with them for the first 24 hours. They should rest, avoid alcohol until they feel better, and avoid contact sport for 3 weeks. Get urgent medical advice if they've been sick once, feel dizzy, take blood thinners, or had been drinking; if told to go to hospital, don't drive yourself. Call emergency services if they were knocked out and haven't woken, can't stay awake, have a seizure, vomit more than once, fell more than 1 metre or 5 stairs, were hit at high speed, have problems seeing, hearing, speaking, walking or with balance, new weakness or numbness, clear fluid from the ears or nose, bleeding from the ears, or changed behaviour.

Source: St John Ambulance (UK), Spinal injury; St John Ambulance (UK), Head injury; St John Ambulance (UK), CPR; British Heart Foundation, How to do CPR; St John Ambulance (UK), Recovery position; NHS, Head injury and concussion; British Red Cross, Head injury; healthdirect (AU), Head injuries. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.

Kyrgyzstan is extremely mountainous, with 94% of its land above 1,000 meters and dominated by the Tien Shan range, including many tall peaks, glaciers, and high-altitude lakes [4].

st-boar-factbook-002.text: Malta is an island in the Mediterranean, approximately 120 km (75 miles) long and 40 km (25 miles) wide. Its capital is Valletta [5]. According to legend, the name "Thimphu" comes from the Dzongkha word "Thimphu," meaning "the place where the lion king rested," symbolizing strength and sovereignty.

st-boar-factbook-015.text: Guatemala faces volcanic risks due to its location in a tectonic boundary zone with active volcanoes in the Sierra Madre range, such as Pacaya and Fuego, which have frequent eruptions [1]. It also faces storm risks, especially on the Caribbean coast, due to its exposure to hurricanes and tropical storms [1]. Among the volcanoes, Pacaya is one of the most active, with eruptions since 1965, and Santa Maria is a Decade Volcano due to its explosive history and proximity to human populations [1].

st-boar-factbook-019.text: The Maldives has the lowest land elevation of any country, with its islands rising only a few meters above sea level, making them highly vulnerable to sea level rise and tsunamis [4]. In contrast, the Seychelles have higher land elevations, with most of their landmass above sea level, and are outside the cyclone belt, experiencing rare severe storms but occasional droughts [3]. Both face climate-related risks, but the Maldives is more directly threatened by rising seas.

st-boar-factbook-020.text: Ireland does not produce more per person than Austria; Austria has a higher GDP per capita. Austria’s landscapes are dominated by mountainous terrain, including the Alps with peaks like Grossglockner (2,590 m), while Ireland is mostly flat to rolling, with its highest point being Carrauntoohil at 1,041 m [8].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-001.text: Heat cannot flow by itself from a cold object to a warmer one because that would violate the principle of energy conservation and the natural direction of entropy increase. Rudolf Clausius stated it as "Heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder to a hotter body," while Lord Kelvin (William Thomson) formulated it as "It is impossible for heat to pass from a colder to a warmer body without external work." [2]

st-boar-simplewiki-en-002.text: The Standard Model doesn't include gravity, dark matter, or explain the accelerating expansion of the universe [2]. Physicists address these gaps through theories like quantum gravity, supersymmetry, and extensions to the Standard Model, though no complete solution has been confirmed.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-003.text: Cosmogony focuses on the origin of the universe, such as the Big Bang or the formation of the Solar System, while cosmology studies the universe's structure, evolution, and large-scale phenomena. Science cannot describe the very first instant of the universe because no theory of quantum gravity exists to explain physics at the Planck time, where known laws break down [1].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-004.text: In mechanics, one joule is defined as the work done when a force of one newton moves an object one meter: 1 J = 1 N × 1 m [1]. It relates to the watt as one watt equals one joule per second (1 W = 1 J/s), meaning power is energy transferred per unit time [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-005.text: The Atacama Desert gets almost no rain because it lies in a rain shadow formed by the Andes mountains to the east and the ocean to the west, and its cold, dry air prevents moisture from settling [1]. People collect water by capturing fog, which collects on plastic surfaces and drips into pans, providing water for drinking and crops [1].

Its rain caused significant flooding and disruption in Spain, particularly in the Madeira Islands, southern Portugal, and southwestern Spain, marking one of the first major storms to impact the region since 1842.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-007.text: In 793, Viking raiders attacked Lindisfarne, destroying the monastery and tearing off the bejeweled cover of the Gospels [4]. After the raid, the monks fled the island and transported the body of Saint Cuthbert to Durham Cathedral, where it was later buried [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-008.text: The English government settled Scots and English people in Ulster during the 17th century to suppress resistance to English rule, particularly from Gaelic Irish chieftains like the O'Neill and O'Donnell dynasties [2]. Settlers were granted land confiscated from Irish clans, and while specific conditions are not detailed in the sources, the colonization was part of a broader policy to establish English control and stability in the region.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-009.text: The Fatimid Caliphate lost its lands due to internal fragmentation, declining military strength, and external pressures, particularly from the Zirid dynasty, which rejected Fatimid rule by 1041 and aligned with the Abbasids. Its final decline was accelerated by the rise of the Ayyubids, who defeated the Fatimids in 1171. The caliphate officially ended when Saladin, leader of the Ayyubid dynasty, captured Cairo and deposed the last Fatimid caliph in 1171, marking the end of Fatimid rule [3].

st-boar-simplewiki-en-010.text: Banks manipulated the Libor rate by submitting falsely low or high interest rates to appear more financially stable or to profit from trades, often through collusion [1]. In response, Britain transferred oversight of Libor to UK regulators, implemented the Wheatley Review reforms, requiring banks to base submissions on actual interbank transactions, publish rates after three months, and introduced criminal penalties for manipulation [2].

This variation fascinated Darwin, as it provided early evidence of how species evolve in response to environmental pressures, forming the basis of his theory of evolution by natural selection.

st-boar-simplewiki-en-012.text: There are about 10 times as many microbial cells as human cells in the body, especially in the gut [1]. The handie-talkie, developed by Motorola during WWII, was hand-held and significantly more portable, though it had a reduced range compared to the original model [1]. The terms are often confused, but the handie-talkie specifically referred to the handheld version [1].
